blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (The switch to Paylane has no way back) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (The nightly settlement worker fails unseen) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The Stripe client is deleted and replaced by the Paylane client in the same
release. There is no switch between the two: keeping both would double the
code to maintain. The Stripe account is closed the day after the release.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: All traffic moves at deploy
findings.recommendation: Keep a way back until Paylane is proven in production: keep the Stripe client behind a configuration switch (provider selected per environment, flipped without a release), and keep the Stripe account open until a stated exit criterion is met (for example N days of Paylane payments with an error rate under a threshold). Write the rollback procedure in the design. Failure scenario: Paylane starts failing authorizations or captures after the release (outage, integration bug, account suspended); the next deploy is about a week away, and redeploying the previous blue version sends payments to a Stripe account already closed — so no card payment can be taken at all, and the operator has no switch to flip.
findings.title: The switch to Paylane has no way back

findings.evidence:
A new worker, `settlement-worker`, runs at 02:00, fetches the day's Paylane
payments and matches them to orders. It runs as a Kubernetes CronJob and
writes its result to the database.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: A worker settles payments nightly
findings.recommendation: Decide in the design how an operator learns that a run failed or did not run: a structured log at start and end of each run (run date, payments fetched, matched, unmatched), a metric or heartbeat for the last successful run, and an alert when a run fails or no successful run is recorded by a deadline. Add the matching task to tasks.md. Failure scenario: the Paylane API is unreachable at 02:00, or the CronJob is never scheduled (bad manifest, suspended job); the worker exits or never starts, nothing is written, and the only alert the spec defines — the finance-channel alert for an unmatched payment — never fires, so a missed settlement looks exactly like a night where everything matched.
findings.title: The nightly settlement worker fails unseen
